Comment LUNCH and I’ll send you links and discounts to my favorite lunch gear! 

And if you’re thinking “it’s too early for back to school…” know that 48% of US schools start *BEFORE* August 16th! 😱 

❄️ WHY TWO ICE PACKS? ❄️
I know you might have eaten warm bologna sandwiches growing up and were just fine, but the official food safety rule is to send packed lunches with 2 sources of ice if they won’t be refrigerated at school.

Perishable foods (meat, poultry, fish, dairy, cut up produce like any cut fruits or veggies, leftovers) are not supposed to be in the temperature danger zone (40-140F) for more than 4 hours for the life of that food. That includes the time it’s in your grocery cart, sitting on your counter at home, etc. Food borne-pathogens are more likely to grow if that food spends a lot of time in that danger zone.

Sending lunch with 2 ice sources (like one ice pack on the top, one on the bottom inside an insulated bag) helps ensure that all perishable items in that lunch stay at a safe temperature. 

If you don’t want to mess with ice packs, use a @Packitcool bag! These are my favorite because you put the entire thing in the freezer. The bag BECOMES the ice packs.

🔥 What if I want to send HOT food? 🔥

There are certain insulated lunch containers that allow you to keep food hot, like the @omielife box, the @bentgo Stainless Steel Food Jar and many @thermosbrand products. To use, add boiling water to the container and let it sit for 10 minutes before adding your hot food. Then pour out the water and add your food. BUT…

MOST PARENTS DON’T REALIZE THIS ➡️ To stay at a safe temperature, the food you put in these insulated hot containers has to be SAUCY (like a saucy pasta or soup). Chicken nuggets will not be hot by lunch time because they’re not saucy enough. It has to have an high liquid content to actually stay hot. ➡️ Also, if there are other perishable foods in that lunch like cut up fruits and veggies, they still need to be sent with ice packs.

Now do you see why I almost always send cold lunches? The temperature thing is tricky 😭

Ddg5kxcGyjv.caption:
thriveafterbabywithalex

There is such a specific kind of heartbreak in looking at your older child after bringing home a baby and thinking:

I miss you.

Not because they went anywhere.

But because you can’t be with them in the same way anymore.

Suddenly someone else is holding them while you feed the baby. Someone else is doing bedtime. You’re saying “one second” and “after I’m done feeding the baby” approximately 900 times a day.

And then you see an old picture of the two of you before the baby was born and it hits you:

They used to have all of me.

Cue the guilt spiral.

Did I change their life too much?
Do they feel pushed aside?
Am I missing this version of them?
Do they know how desperately I still love them?

And maybe the hardest part is that you can’t even fully let yourself grieve it because this is the baby you wanted.

But loving what your family has become doesn’t mean you can’t miss what it used to be.

There is grief inside so many beautiful transitions.

You didn’t stop loving your older child when your baby arrived.

You’re learning how to be their mom in a completely new version of your family.

And that can be beautiful and brutal and tender and really fucking hard all at once. 🤍

Tell me I’m not the only one: did you miss your older child after having another baby?

⁨	התחלת מוצקים זו תקופה של למידה, התנסות והיכרות עם עולם חדש של טעמים, מרקמים וחוויות.
אלו הדברים שהייתי שמה עליהם הכי הרבה דגש❤️⁩

⁨	הזמן המומלץ להתחלת מוצקים הוא סביב גיל 6 חודשים, יחד עם הופעת סימני מוכנות. 
לפני כן, רוב התינוקות אינם מוכנים מבחינה התפתחותית, ומערכת העיכול שלהם עדיין אינה בשלה מספיק.

נחפש סימני מוכנות כמו סקרנות ועניין באוכל, החזקה יציבה של הראש והצוואר, יכולת לשבת עם תמיכה ועוד⁩

⁨	⁨	תינוקות לומדים דרך התנסות.
תנו להם להחזיק, לגעת, למעוך, להכניס לפה- להיות חלק פעיל בארוחה ולהוביל אותה. 

אכילה עצמאית מאפשרת להם לתרגל מיומנויות מוטוריות, להכיר את המזון בקצב שלהם ולצבור ביטחון סביב האכילה.⁩⁩

⁨	זה לא בלגן- זו התפתחות!
לכלוך בזמן האוכל הוא שלב הכרחי בלמידה המוטורית, התחושתית והרגשית שלהם.⁩

⁨	ההתנסות במרקמים שונים ומגוונים היא חלק חשוב מתהליך הלמידה של לעיסה ואכילה.⁩

⁨	הושבה נכונה היא קריטית גם לבטיחות וגם לנוחות בזמן הארוחה.

מושיבים זקוף עם כלל ה-90-90-90: 90 מעלות בירכיים, בברכיים ובקרוסליים. 

אכילה בשיפוע (כמו בטרמפולינה/סלקל/עגלה וכדומה) אינה מומלצת ומעלה סיכון לחנק.⁩

⁨	תינוקות לומדים ומתקדמים בצורה הטובה ביותר פשוט מלראות אותנו אוכלים.

ככל שמתאפשר, נסו לצרף אותם לארוחות המשפחתיות- לשבת יחד סביב השולחן, לראות אתכם אוכלים ולחוות את הארוחה כחלק טבעי ונעים מהיום.⁩

⁨	האווירה בזמן הארוחה משפיעה על החוויה של התינוק, ועל היחס שלו לאוכל בהמשך.

נסו להימנע מלחץ, שכנועים והסחות דעת.
תהיו קשובים לסימני הרעב והשובע של התינוק ותאפשרו לו להתקדם בקצב שלו.⁩

Always reminding. Always rushing. Snapping over little things because my brain was already full.

Then feeling guilty because I wanted to enjoy my kids, but I was spending so much of the day managing everyone.

Even when someone helped, I still had to notice, remember, explain, and ask. I wanted things off my brain, too.

So we RESET our household.

My husband and I sat down and made a plan together. Clear responsibilities. Meals planned ahead. Screen rules we BOTH followed. Checklists the kids could use without asking Mom what came next.

And we had to change, too. Teach them. Set things up so they could succeed. Let them take longer without jumping in and taking over.

These changes gave our kids more independence—and gave me room to breathe.

If you’re tired of having the same arguments, repeating the same instructions, and ending every day with nothing left, this is what we’ll work on together in the Family Reset Challenge.

A plan for YOUR family, built around what matters to you, with everyone knowing their part.

One thing we’ve always been intentional about is giving our kids responsibilities early. Not because they’re going to do them perfectly, but because they’ll never learn if we don’t let them start.

The truth is, my kids don’t do everything in this carousel perfectly. They still forget things for practice. Laundry still comes out wrinkled sometimes. The kitchen is definitely messier after they make breakfast. 😂 But every time they do it, they get a little better.

I think a lot of parents don’t start because it feels easier to just do it ourselves. And honestly, in the beginning, it probably is. Teaching a 5-year-old takes more time than doing it for them.

But I don’t think about this week. I think about the next 10 years.

Every skill they learn now is one less thing they’ll have to figure out when they’re older. More importantly, every time they accomplish something on their own, they build confidence. They start believing, “I can do hard things.”

At the end of the day, I’m not trying to raise kids who do everything perfectly. I’m trying to raise capable, confident adults. And that starts with letting them practice while they’re still young.

What’s one responsibility your kids have that surprises other parents? I’d love to hear it in the comments. 💛

I read about this “experiment” in Sally Goddard Blythe’s book The Well Balanced Child years ago, and I haven’t been able to get it out of my brain.

I just always think about…what if we could get every school in the country doing this?

What could that look like for learning? For motor skills? Or even for mental health?!

We ask SO much of kids’ brains during the school day: pay attention, sit still, read, write, remember, regulate impulses, but sometimes we forget that these skills live at the TOP of the developmental pyramid.

They depend on a firm foundation built through early movement, rich sensory experiences and the natural maturation of motor skills, things modern childhood can so easily interfere with.

Movement isn’t time taken away from learning. Done intentionally, it can help prepare and shape the brain to learn to it’s FULLEST potential.

And while changing every school in the country might be a lofty goal, we CAN start small.

These same types of developmental movements can be woven into a child’s day at home or in the classroom and they don’t require fancy equipment or hours of extra time.
